_comment: Which columns the LOADER controls, and at what rate.
READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A COLUMN HERE. Only two columns belong in this
file, because only two are things the loader invents or suppresses. Every
other field is carried VERBATIM from the CSVs, and must stay that way.
The Lexington CSVs are a SUBSET OF THE PARTNER CORPUS, not an independent
extraction -- verified 2026-08-05 by pulling the same people out of
production over the indexed (last_name, zip) path. The residents our CSVs
place at 1104 SPRING RUN RD are present in production at the same address,
in the same feeds, and the rows match field for field. So a CSV value IS
production's value, and down-sampling one can only move the clone AWAY from
production. An earlier revision of this file calibrated dob/phone/email
toward feed_id_coverage and was measurably deleting real data:
production  TAMIE WORTHINGTON  dob=1968-01-01
clone       TAMIE WORTHINGTON  dob=(deleted by the sampler)
feed_id_coverage is also a NATIONAL per-feed average, so calibrating a
Lexington subset against it imported a second error on top of the first.
WHAT REMAINS, and why each is still legitimate:
ssn          Our CSVs carry none at all, so it cannot be copied -- it is
synthesised (identity.py, 900-999 area range, never issued by
the SSA). The RATE matters because ssn is production's entity
blocking key: populating it only on the payday feeds is what
makes entity_links skew to records_new and leaves tax
unlinked, exactly as production does, emergently.
house_number Our CSVs carry it on trace/auto/tax where production has it
NULL -- the old cleaning pipeline parsed it out of the address
text; production never stored it for those feeds. Gating it to
base/USCRM restores production's reality. It is also the
resident hop's only anchor, so getting this wrong silently
disables the hop (it did once: every value dropped, zero
anchors, 10 of 12 benchmark addresses unresolvable).
0.0 means production genuinely has none. 100.0 means keep every value.
